title: Abu Jandal’s Chains • ‘Umar’s Question • The Days After the Treaty • Three Commanders from Quraysh’s House

blocks.1: The treaty had not yet been fully written. Suddenly, stumbling in chains on his feet, Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl arrived, Suhayl’s own son. He had escaped from the lower side of Makkah, and came and fell down among the Muslims. Suhayl said, Muhammad, this is the first condition about which I am making a pact with you; return him. The Prophet {{1}} said, we have not yet finished writing. Suhayl said, then by Allah, I will not make peace with you on anything. The Prophet {{2}} said, release him for my sake. Suhayl said, I will not. Abu Jandal (RA) cried out,
blocks.3: O Muslims, I have come as a Muslim, and still I am to be returned to the polytheists? Do you not see what I have suffered?{{1}}
blocks.4: The narrator says, he had been tortured severely in the way of Allah. Yet he had to go back.{{1}}
blocks.5: The Prophet {{1}} said to him, Abu Jandal, be patient, hope for reward; Allah will bring out a way of release for you and for the weak ones with you. We have made peace with them, given our word in Allah’s name, we will not betray them.{{2}}
blocks.6: Before his own eyes a Muslim brother had to be sent back with his chains. Had he broken his word that day no one would have blamed the Prophet {{1}}; on the contrary everyone would have said, he took the side of the oppressed. Yet the word was kept. Because keeping a given word never depends on convenience.
blocks.7: In our lives too there are words which, if broken, no one would know, no one would even blame us, on the contrary we would gain. That is exactly where one can tell whether I keep the word out of fear of people or for Allah.
blocks.9: Seeing the terms, seeing Abu Jandal sent back, the Companions’ hearts grew heavy. ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) went to the Prophet {{1}}.
blocks.11: Are you not truly the Prophet of Allah? He said, certainly. ‘Umar said, are we not on the truth and the enemy on falsehood? He said, certainly. ‘Umar said, then why should we accept this humiliation in our religion? He said, I am the Messenger of Allah, I do not disobey Him, and He is my helper. ‘Umar said, did you not tell us that we would go to the Ka‘bah and perform tawaf? He said, I did; but did I say, this very year? ‘Umar said, no. He said, you will go there, and you will perform tawaf.{{1}}
blocks.12: ‘Umar (RA) then went to Abu Bakr (RA) and asked the same questions. Abu Bakr (RA) gave exactly the same answers, then said, hold fast to his stirrup; by Allah, he is on the truth. ‘Umar (RA) used to say later, for those words of that day I performed many deeds.{{1}}
blocks.13: Even in the heart of the one whose faith is firmest, questions arise. Questions arising is no fault; the fault is not accepting after getting the answer. ‘Umar (RA) asked, accepted the answer, and made atonement for his haste with deeds.
blocks.14: And Abu Bakr’s (RA) answer was an exact echo of the Prophet’s {{1}} answer. When trust is this deep, on hearing the question one can tell what the answer will be.
blocks.15: The ‘Fath’ (Victory) That Descended on That Very Journey
blocks.16: On the way back, ‘Umar (RA) himself told of one night. He was travelling beside the Prophet {{1}} on a journey. He asked a question three times; the Prophet {{2}} did not answer even once. ‘Umar (RA) scolded himself, may ‘Umar’s mother lose you, you pestered the Messenger of Allah {{3}} three times, and did not get an answer even once! He spurred his camel and went ahead of the Muslims. He feared lest a Qur’anic revelation come down about him. Hardly a little time had passed when someone began to call him. ‘Umar (RA) thought, surely a revelation has come down about him. He went to the Prophet {{4}} and gave salam. The Prophet {{5}} said,
blocks.18: Tonight a surah has been revealed to me. It is dearer to me than everything on which the sun rises.{{1}}
blocks.19: Then he recited, Inna fatahna laka fathan mubina. The Qur’an says like this,
blocks.21: (O Messenger!) Know for certain that We have granted you a clear victory, so that Allah may forgive your past and future faults, complete His favour upon you and guide you on a straight path; and (so that Allah) may help you with a help that prevails over all.{{1}}
blocks.22: The journey that many thought a defeat, the very name of its surah is ‘Victory’.{{1}}
blocks.23: We pass judgment on seeing the headline; loss, defeat, failure. Yet the journey that many had thought a defeat, the very name of its surah is ‘Victory’. What is now seeming a loss, what its name is in Allah’s reckoning, we do not know. The Qur’an did not hide the Companions’ state of mind either. With faces full of grief and sorrow they said, we have come to know what Allah will do about you; what about us? Then the next verses came down: for believing men and women, gardens beneath which rivers flow. The grief did not have to be held in. The Qur’an recorded the words of the Companions’ sorrowful faces, and sent glad tidings along with it. We hide the pain of the heart, or pour it out to the wrong people. Those who were able to tell their pain to Allah, their answer came. And the Qur’an also reminded of the dream. Before the journey the Prophet {{1}} had seen in a dream that he was entering al-Masjid al-Haram with the Companions. Did that dream turn out false? The Qur’an informed,
blocks.25: Indeed Allah showed His Messenger the true dream, which was entirely real. You will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram in safety, with (some of) you having your heads shaved and (some) with hair cut short, without fear. Allah knows what you do not know. So before the fulfilment of that dream He ordained a nearby victory.{{1}}
blocks.26: The time was not stated in the dream. ‘This very year’ was our own reckoning. Allah’s word comes true in Allah’s time. The next year that dream was fulfilled; the nearby victory was Khaybar.
blocks.28: When the writing of the treaty was done the Prophet {{1}} said, rise, sacrifice, shave your heads. No one rose. He said it three times, still no one. Everyone’s heart was broken. The Prophet {{2}} went to Umm Salamah (RA) and told her what had happened. She said, go out without saying anything to anyone, sacrifice your own animal, call a barber and have your head shaved. The Prophet {{3}} did exactly that. The moment they saw it everyone rose and sacrificed, and began to shave one another’s heads, as if in grief they would kill one another.{{4}}
blocks.29: Where saying a thing again and again does not work, doing it oneself and showing it works. And on one wife’s one counsel that day a great crisis passed; there is nothing to belittle in the words of the people of one’s household. The Companions sacrificed one camel for seven persons; a cow also for seven. Among his own animals the Prophet {{1}} placed one camel of Abu Jahl, which had a silver ring in its nose. The aim was to anger the polytheists. The chief’s camel is today among the sacrificial animals of Allah’s House.{{2}}
blocks.30: Then the Prophet {{1}} made du‘a for those who had shaved their heads. The Companions said, and those who cut their hair short? He again made du‘a for those who shaved. The Companions said it again. The fourth time he said, for those who cut short too.
blocks.32: May Allah have mercy on those who shave their heads.{{1}}
blocks.33: At first only the names of those who shaved. The Companions spoke up, and those who cut their hair short? He did not discard this word of the Companions, in the end he included them too in the du‘a. He respected the words of the Companions’ mouths. When we are grown we discard the words of the young; of a child, of a subordinate, of a new colleague. We set aside, saying we will listen later. The Prophet {{1}} listened up to the fourth time, until the Companions’ word found a place inside the du‘a. On that very journey a Companion had a head infested with lice. Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah (RA) was suffering while in ihram. The Prophet {{2}} saw and said, are the lice on your head troubling you? He said, yes.
blocks.35: Shave your head. Then fast three days, or feed six poor people, or sacrifice one sheep.{{1}}
blocks.36: Shaving the head is forbidden in ihram. But because of hardship that too was relaxed, with an easy path of fidyah. That verse of al-Baqarah came down in this very situation of Hudaybiyah; what the rule is for people halted by obstruction is also stated there. An easy path had been kept within the rule itself for hardship. Sometimes we place on ourselves such severity as is not a command. Where an easy path is open there is nothing in adding hardship of our own invention. In the terms of the treaty was the matter of returning men. Now women came. Some believing women migrated from Makkah and came to Madinah; their relatives came and asked for them back, citing the condition. The Prophet {{1}} did not return them. Because the language of the condition was for men. And now the Qur’an itself gave the instruction,
blocks.38: O you who believe! When believing women come to you as emigrants, test them. Allah knows best their faith. Then if you know them to be believers, do not send them back to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for the disbelievers, nor are the disbelievers lawful for them.{{1}}
blocks.39: The conditions of that test the Qur’an has told like this,
blocks.41: O Prophet! When believing women come to you to pledge allegiance that they will not associate anything with Allah, will not steal, will not commit adultery, will not kill their children, will not bring any slander that they fabricate between their hands and feet, and will not disobey you in anything good, then accept their pledge and ask Allah’s forgiveness for them. Surely Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.{{1}}
blocks.42: No shirk, no theft, no adultery, no killing of children, no false slander, no disobedience in good. The test of a woman’s faith is the measure of her character. The test of women was the pledge by word of mouth. ‘A’ishah (RA) said, the Prophet’s {{1}} hand never touched any woman’s hand; he only said in words, I have taken your pledge. Another change came inside the home. ‘Umar (RA) that day divorced his two polytheist wives. Later Mu‘awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married one, and Safwan ibn Umayyah the other. As soon as the Qur’anic command came down, even the closest bond was let go.{{2}}
blocks.43: A person whose name is not on the paper of the pact can be endangered by the force of letters. The Prophet {{1}} kept the letter of the condition, but did not return people who were not caught by the letter. The person who is not on the paper of our dealings, is he absent from our conscience too?
blocks.45: After returning to Madinah, Abu Basir (RA) of Quraysh became Muslim and escaped and came. Behind him Quraysh sent two men; reminded of the pact. The Prophet {{1}} handed him over to them. Reaching Dhu al-Hulayfah they sat down to eat dates. Abu Basir (RA) said to one, by Allah, your sword seems excellent. The man drew it from the scabbard and said, yes, I have tested it many times. Abu Basir said, let me see it a little. As soon as it was in his hand he struck him; the man lay dead right there. The other ran away, reached Madinah and ran into the mosque. The Prophet {{2}} said on seeing him, this one has seen something frightening. The man said, by Allah, my companion has been killed, and he will kill me too. Behind him came Abu Basir (RA) and said, O Prophet of Allah, Allah has fulfilled your obligation; you did indeed return me, then Allah saved me from their hands. The Prophet {{3}} said,
blocks.47: Woe to his mother! A kindler of war; if only he had someone with him!{{1}}
blocks.48: Hearing the words, Abu Basir (RA) understood that he would be sent back again. He went out, straight to the seashore. The Prophet {{1}} could not keep him in Madinah, because of the treaty; yet he did not punish him either. In one sentence he made it understood: there is no place here, but you are not alone. Keeping the letter of the treaty, and keeping the way of the oppressed open from within it; both together. Abu Jandal (RA) too rushed from Makkah and joined him. After that whoever of Quraysh became Muslim went and joined them there. Slowly a band came to stand; the caravans of Quraysh going toward Sham they would block. In the end Quraysh themselves, appealing in the name of Allah and kinship, sent word to the Prophet {{2}}; call them in, from now on whoever comes to you is safe.{{3}}
blocks.49: The condition that had first seemed most one-sided, in the end Quraysh themselves asked to have it taken back. The pact was not broken, yet a way came out; that word given to Abu Jandal, Allah will bring out a way, came true.
blocks.51: The Treaty of Hudaybiyah bent the backbone of Quraysh. And in the very days after that treaty three of Makkah’s sharpest men found their own way: ‘Amr ibn al-‘As, Khalid ibn al-Walid and ‘Uthman ibn Talhah. ‘Amr’s story begins earlier, after the Trench. He was then Quraysh’s diplomat. He went to the Najashi of Habashah, with a scheme. There was the Prophet’s {{1}} envoy ‘Amr ibn Umayyah. He told his companions, I will ask for him and cut off his neck. The Najashi, hearing it, grew angry. He said,
blocks.53: Do you ask me to hand over to you the envoy of a man to whom comes the great Namus, the one who used to come to Musa, so that you may kill him? ‘Amr, listen to me, follow him. By Allah, he is surely on the truth.{{1}}
blocks.54: ‘Amr (RA) himself said, hearing this, everything changed inside me. I said, will you take my pledge on his behalf, for Islam? The Najashi said, yes. He stretched out his hand, I pledged for Islam. From his companions he hid his Islam. Then he set out toward the Prophet {{1}}, to accept Islam. On the way he met Khalid ibn al-Walid. A little before the conquest of Makkah. Khalid was coming from the direction of Makkah, the Khalid who on the day of Uhud was leader of Quraysh’s horsemen. ‘Amr said, Abu Sulayman, where? Khalid said,
blocks.56: By Allah, the road has become straight. The man is certainly a prophet. I am going, by Allah, to accept Islam. How much longer?{{1}}
blocks.57: ‘Amr said, I too have come to accept Islam. The two reached Madinah together. ‘Uthman ibn Talhah was with them too.{{1}}
blocks.58: Khalid went forward first to the Prophet {{1}}. He accepted Islam, pledged. Then ‘Amr. He said, O Messenger of Allah, I will pledge on the condition that my earlier sins are forgiven; I do not speak of what comes after. The Prophet {{2}} said,
blocks.60: ‘Amr, pledge. Islam wipes out all that was before it, and hijrah wipes out all that was before it.{{1}}
blocks.62: Those who had once raised swords against the Prophet {{1}} came and stood before him. The past became a burden to no one. Islam gave a chance to begin anew. These three did not say the same thing. ‘Amr found the way in the Najashi’s anger. Khalid found it in his own conscience. But on the lips of both there was one phrase: how much longer? We too grasp the truth. But about accepting it we let the days lie, saying we will do it later. In the uproar of battle truth does not enter the ear; in the days of peace the heart learns to listen. The fruit of the treaty is not only on the paper of terms, but in the hearts of these people.

Note 1: according to the sahih narrations this verse was revealed after the Treaty of Hudaybiyah; on the face of it the terms of the treaty cannot be called a clear victory, but considering the situation it is the background of the great victory, in the end Makkah will be conquered. Note 3: ‘the straight path’ means that the obstruction that had been on the path of spreading the religion from the disbelievers until now will be removed after this victory.
footnotes.7: Sahih al-Bukhari 4177, 4833 (from ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)): on the journey at night, asking three times and not receiving the Prophet’s {{1}} answer, ‘I feared lest a Qur’anic revelation come down about me’; ‘Tonight a surah has been revealed to me, dearer to me than that on which the sun rises’, then he recited ‘Inna fatahna laka fathan mubina’. Sahih Muslim 1786 (Anas (RA): Surah al-Fath was revealed on the way back from Hudaybiyah, the Companions then overcome with grief and sorrow, having done the sacrifice at Hudaybiyah itself; the Prophet {{2}} said, ‘a verse has been revealed to me which is dearer to me than everything in the world’; the Companions said, ‘we have come to know what will be done with you, what about us?’, then 48:5 was revealed; Ahmad 13246, al-Arna’ut: sahih on the condition of the two Shaykhs). Al-Rahiq, p. 569.
footnotes.8: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 3, Surah al-Fath 48:27, p. 378 (read from the printed page). Note 29 (p. 378): before the journey of Hudaybiyah the Prophet {{1}} had seen in a dream that he was entering al-Masjid al-Haram with the Companions, hence the departure for ‘umrah; when after the treaty ihram had to be removed, some had misgivings; the verse informed that the dream is true, but the time had not been specified; it was fulfilled the next year. Note 30: ‘the nearby victory’ is Khaybar.
footnotes.9: Sahih al-Bukhari 2731–2732 (the command to sacrifice, the Companions’ hesitation, Umm Salamah (RA)’s counsel).
footnotes.10: Sahih Muslim 1318 (Jabir (RA): ‘in the year of Hudaybiyah we sacrificed one camel for seven and one cow for seven’). Ahmad 15259: seventy camels were slaughtered (al-Arna’ut: hasan). Abu Dawud 1749 (Ibn ‘Abbas (RA): in the year of Hudaybiyah the Prophet {{1}} sent among the sacrificial animals one camel of Abu Jahl, which had a silver ring in its nose, ‘to anger the polytheists’; in the chain ‘sakata ‘anhu’, al-Albani: hasan; with the word ‘silver’, not ‘gold’). Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 563–564.
footnotes.11: Sahih al-Bukhari 1727 (from Ibn ‘Umar (RA): ‘May Allah have mercy on those who shave their heads’; the Companions said, ‘and those who cut short?’; he said the same again; the Companions said it again; he said, ‘and those who cut short too’). Al-Bukhari 1728 has the same in Abu Hurayrah’s narration. Al-Rahiq, pp. 563–564.
footnotes.12: Sahih al-Bukhari 1814 (from Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah (RA): ‘Are the lice on your head troubling you? Yes. Then the Prophet {{1}} said, shave your head, and fast three days, or feed six poor people, or sacrifice one sheep’). Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 1, Surah al-Baqarah 2:196, p. 121 and notes 126–127: this verse was revealed in the situation of being obstructed at Hudaybiyah. Al-Rahiq, p. 564 (the incident of Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah, ‘on this very journey’).
footnotes.13: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 3, Surah al-Mumtahanah 60:10, pp. 528–529 (read from the printed page). Note 5 (p. 529): a Muslim woman cannot remain in the marriage of a non-Muslim man; if the husband does not accept Islam within the ‘iddah the marriage is annulled. Note 6: since there was then a treaty with Makkah, there was the opportunity to ask back the mahr that had been given to the wives.
footnotes.14: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 3, Surah al-Mumtahanah 60:12, p. 531 (read from the printed page). Note 10: ‘fabricating slander between their hands and feet’ is an Arabic idiom; two explanations: knowingly slandering someone falsely, or passing off a child begotten by another as one’s husband’s child. Sahih al-Bukhari 2711, 4891 (‘A’ishah (RA): the Prophet {{1}} used to test the emigrant women with this verse).
footnotes.15: Sahih al-Bukhari 2731–2732 (through al-Miswar and Marwan, the part after the treaty: ‘then some believing women came; Allah revealed “O you who believe, when believing women come to you as emigrants, test them” up to “do not hold on to the ties of the disbelieving women”; that day ‘Umar divorced his two wives who were polytheists; one of them was married by Mu‘awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, the other by Safwan ibn Umayyah’). Bukhari 2711, 4891 (‘A’ishah (RA): the Prophet {{1}} used to test the women with Surah al-Mumtahanah 60:12; ‘By Allah, his hand never touched any woman’s hand at the time of pledge; he used to take the pledge only in words’). Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 564–565.
footnotes.16: Sahih al-Bukhari 2731–2732 (through al-Miswar and Marwan; asking to see the sword at Dhu al-Hulayfah, killing one, the other’s running into the mosque, ‘this one has seen something frightening’, Abu Basir’s ‘Allah has fulfilled your obligation’, and ‘waylu ummihi mis‘ara harbin law kana lahu ahad’). ‘Waylu ummihi’ is, in Arabic, a manner of speech mixing amazement and praise, not a curse.
footnotes.17: The end part of Sahih al-Bukhari 2731–2732 (the refuge of Abu Basir and Abu Jandal (RA) on the seashore, Quraysh’s request).
footnotes.18: Musnad Ahmad 17777 (‘Amr ibn al-‘As (RA)’s own narration), the Najashi’s words are quoted from this narration in Ibn Kathir’s al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah. By ‘al-Namus al-Akbar’ is meant Jibril (AS), the angel of revelation. Grade of the chain: hasan in Irwa’ al-Ghalil 5/122.
footnotes.19: Musnad Ahmad 17777 (from ‘Amr ibn al-‘As (RA)): ‘A little before the conquest of Makkah I met Khalid ibn al-Walid, he was coming from the direction of Makkah; I said, Abu Sulayman, where? He said, ...’. ‘Mansim’ (a path like a camel’s claw) and in some chains the word ‘maysam’; the meaning, the direction of the road has become clear.
footnotes.20: Sirah-based: the Islam of ‘Uthman ibn Talhah (keeper of the Ka‘bah’s key, of Banu ‘Abd al-Dar): Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 571 (‘Amr, Khalid and ‘Uthman presented themselves together in the Prophet’s {{1}} court). In Ahmad’s hadith the names of Khalid and ‘Amr are there, ‘Uthman’s is not. In this dars only ‘with them’ is said.
footnotes.21: Musnad Ahmad 17777; al-Albani, Sahih al-Jami‘ 1329 (‘Islam wipes out all before it, and hijrah, and hajj’: sahih). ‘Amr (RA)’s condition was: ‘that my earlier sins be forgiven; I do not speak of what comes after’.
footnotes.22: Musnad Ahmad 17777 (‘Amr ibn al-‘As (RA)’s own narration, through Habib ibn Abi Aws); al-Albani, Irwa’ al-Ghalil 5/122: ‘hasan or close’; al-‘Ala’i, Majmu‘ Rasa’il 4/191 and 2/280: sahih. Ibn Kathir, al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah (‘Amr’s first journey to the Najashi after the Trench; their Islam ‘after Hudaybiyah’). The year has not been put in the dars, since there is no agreement on the year.

quiz.q: Whose son was Abu Jandal (RA)?
quiz.e: He was the son of Suhayl, the very one making the treaty.

quiz.q: I have given someone my word, now keeping it is my loss, and no one will know if I break it; what should be done according to this dars?
o: If no one knows, breaking is fine
If there is loss, the word is void
Get someone else to keep the word
Accept the loss and keep the word
quiz.e: The incident of Abu Jandal is the answer.

quiz.q: Which surah did the Prophet ﷺ speak of to ‘Umar (RA) at night?
quiz.e: ‘Tonight a surah has been revealed to me’ (Bukhari 4177).

quiz.q: What becomes clear from ‘Umar’s (RA) questions?
o: Questions arising is no fault, not accepting the answer is the fault
Asking questions is a sign of weak faith
Questions do not arise in the minds of great Companions
The right answer to a question is always found immediately
quiz.e: He asked, accepted the answer, then made atonement in deeds.

quiz.q: In the Prophet’s ﷺ answer ‘did I say, this very year?’, what misunderstanding was corrected?
o: Denying the promise of tawaf altogether
Binding the promise’s time to one’s own assumption
quiz.e: The promise was true; ‘Umar (RA) himself had assumed the time.

quiz.q: Why did ‘Umar (RA) become afraid on asking at night and getting no answer?
o: Because the Prophet ﷺ was angry
Fear of losing the way at night
Fear of a revelation coming down
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 4177.

quiz.q: What does the Tawdih al-Qur’an note say about the dream in Fath 48:27?
o: The dream was fulfilled that very year
The time was not fixed; fulfilled the next year

quiz.q: When a question arises in the mind about the decision of a great person, what is the etiquette according to this dars?
o: Ask directly and accept the answer
Keep the question suppressed and stay quietly displeased
quiz.e: ‘Umar (RA) asked, then accepted.

quiz.q: If the fulfilment of some promise of Allah seems to be coming late, which thing needs to be remembered?
o: The promise itself was perhaps misunderstood
Not binding the time to one’s own assumption
It is better to give up waiting
quiz.e: ‘Did I say, this very year?’

quiz.q: The glad tidings of the journey that many had thought a defeat fit with which event?
quiz.e: The journey many thought a defeat, the very name of its surah is ‘Fath’.

quiz.q: When the Companions hesitated at the command to sacrifice, whose advice did the Prophet ﷺ take?
quiz.e: Umm Salamah (RA) advised, to sacrifice himself and show it.

quiz.q: Where did Abu Basir (RA) finally take refuge?
quiz.e: He took refuge on the seashore.

quiz.q: According to Mumtahanah 60:10, what is the instruction about emigrant women?
o: They must be returned according to the condition, no exemption
If tested and found believers they may not be sent back
If the husband comes to take her, the woman will have the option to go back of her own will
They are to be returned only if the mahr is not returned, otherwise not
quiz.e: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 3, pp. 528–529.

quiz.q: What did ‘Umar (RA) do that day?
o: Returned both women’s mahr to the polytheists
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 2731–2732.

quiz.q: What was sacrificed for seven persons at Hudaybiyah?
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 1318 (Jabir (RA)).

quiz.q: Among the conditions of the women’s pledge in Mumtahanah 60:12, which one is there?
o: Going back to the disbelieving husband
quiz.e: Shirk, theft, adultery, killing children, slander, disobedience in good; Bukhari 4891.

quiz.q: Why did Umm Salamah’s (RA) advice work?
o: The Companions obeyed Umm Salamah more
This time the Prophet ﷺ spoke in harsh words
Doing it oneself and showing draws more than words
The mood lightened because Quraysh had left
quiz.e: As soon as the Prophet ﷺ himself sacrificed, everyone rose.

quiz.q: In the incident of Abu Basir (RA), what was the outcome of the one-sided condition?
o: The Muslims broke the treaty and kept him
The condition was made even stricter
No more questions were raised about the condition
Quraysh themselves asked for the condition to be taken back
quiz.e: Because of obstruction to their caravans, Quraysh themselves asked.

quiz.q: What can be understood from the du‘a for those who cut their hair short, at the Companions’ request?
o: Cutting short is better than shaving
The du‘a is only the right of those who shave
The du‘a was a strict rule
quiz.e: The fourth time he said, for those who cut short too (Bukhari 1727).

quiz.q: From the incident of Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah, what is the ruling on shaving the head in ihram because of hardship?
o: Never to be shaved under any condition
May not shave except after the sacrifice
quiz.e: Fidyah of fasting, charity or sacrifice (Bukhari 1814; Baqarah 2:196).

quiz.q: When one has to accept an apparently one-sided settlement, what hope does this dars give?
o: A one-sided settlement is always ultimately harmful
Settlements should be broken as soon as the chance comes
With patience a way comes out from within
quiz.e: The condition that seemed one-sided, Quraysh themselves asked to have it taken back.

quiz.q: Which is an example of putting Allah’s command before close relationships?
quiz.e: After the Qur’anic command came down, ‘Umar (RA) did exactly that.

quiz.q: If someone is turned away by mistake, finding a way to set it right oneself later fits with which incident?
o: The incident of the ring’s three-line design
quiz.e: From within the condition itself the oppressed one’s way opened.

quiz.q: A little before the conquest of Makkah, on the way to accept Islam, what question did Khalid ibn al-Walid ask ‘Amr ibn al-‘As?
o: Did I say, this very year?
Are we not on the truth?
quiz.e: ‘Fa-hatta mata?’; Ahmad 17777.

quiz.q: Against putting off accepting a truth one has understood, saying ‘I will do it later’, which statement comes to mind?
quiz.e: An example of recognising the truth and not delaying.
